blocks.text: Vocabulary Study — Tissues in Action
1. Word Wall
Meristematic Tissues: Groups of cells that can divide continuously, responsible for plant growth.
Picture: Cells in a plant root tip actively dividing.
Permanent Tissues: Tissues formed from meristematic tissues that have differentiated to perform specific functions.
Picture: Different types of plant cells, such as xylem and phloem.
Epithelial Tissue: Tissue that forms the outer covering of the body and lines internal organs.
Picture: Layer of tightly packed cells protecting underlying tissues.
Connective Tissue: Tissues that support and connect different parts of the body.
Picture: Blood and bone cells providing structure and transport.
Muscular Tissue: Tissue responsible for movement in the body, including skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscles.
Picture: Muscle fibers contracting to enable movement.
Apical Meristem: Meristematic tissue located at the tips of roots and shoots, responsible for growth in length.
Picture: Growth tip of a plant root.
Lateral Meristem: Meristematic tissue responsible for growth in girth, found in the stems of plants.
Picture: Cross-section of a tree trunk showing growth rings.
Intercalary Meristem: Meristematic tissue located at the base of internodes, aiding in regrowth after cutting.
Picture: New grass shoots emerging after being cut.
Xylem: Complex permanent tissue that transports water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.
Picture: Diagram of xylem vessels in a plant.
Phloem: Complex permanent tissue that transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
Picture: Diagram of phloem tissue in a plant.
Skeletal Muscle: Voluntary muscular tissue attached to bones, responsible for body movement.
Picture: Skeletal muscle fibers in action.
Smooth Muscle: Involuntary muscular tissue found in organs, responsible for automatic movements.
Picture: Smooth muscle tissue in the digestive tract.
Cardiac Muscle: Involuntary muscular tissue found in the heart, responsible for pumping blood.
Picture: Cardiac muscle fibers contracting.
2. Flashcards
FRONT: What are meristematic tissues?  →  BACK: Groups of cells that can divide continuously, responsible for plant growth.
FRONT: What is the function of epithelial tissue?  →  BACK: To form the outer covering of the body and line internal organs.
FRONT: What does xylem do?  →  BACK: Transports water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.
FRONT: What is the role of skeletal muscle?  →  BACK: Responsible for voluntary movements of the body.
3. Picture Words
Meristematic Tissues — Green — Draw: A plant root tip with dividing cells.
Xylem — Blue — Draw: Xylem vessels transporting water.
Epithelial Tissue — Yellow — Draw: Layer of epithelial cells.
4. Say · Spell · Use
Meristematic Tissues (/ˌmɛrəˈstɛmətɪk ˈtɪʃuːz/) — ____ are responsible for the growth of plants.
Connective Tissue (/kəˈnɛktɪv ˈtɪʃuː/) — ____ supports and connects different parts of the body.
Apical Meristem (/ˈeɪpɪkəl ˈmɛrəˌstɛm/) — The ____ is located at the tips of roots and shoots.
5. Self-Test
Match the tissue type with its function.
Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.
Epithelial tissue protects underlying tissues and facilitates absorption.
Muscular tissue enables movement in the body.
6. Quick Reference
Epithelial Tissue: Forms the outer covering of the body and lines internal organs. (Exam tip: Focus on types: squamous, cuboidal, columnar.)
Connective Tissue: Supports and connects different parts of the body. (Exam tip: Remember examples: blood, bone, cartilage.)
Muscular Tissue: Responsible for movement in the body. (Exam tip: Differentiate between voluntary and involuntary muscles.)
7. Concept Map
Study how all vocabulary terms connect to the main topic.
Tip: Download the HTML vocabulary file for the full arrow flowchart (best for colour printing).
Tissues in Action

Meristematic Tissues | Permanent Tissues | Epithelial Tissue
Connective Tissue | Muscular Tissue | Apical Meristem
Lateral Meristem | Intercalary Meristem | Xylem
Phloem | Skeletal Muscle | Smooth Muscle
